blocks.text: The chapter begins with “all Israel,” yet its register especially names Judah, Benjamin, priests, Levites, and people connected with Jerusalem. In Chronicles, “all Israel” should not be reduced to a narrow biological category, but neither does it mean that every group was equally represented in every setting. The larger genealogical and administrative record connects the restored community with Israel’s tribes, David, priestly and Levitical offices, and preexilic Jerusalem.

The genealogies leading up to this chapter function as selective maps of kinship, land, office, and restored identity rather than as exhaustive modern-style biological pedigrees. Their gaps, parallel lines, and variant names therefore need to be considered case by case.
